answer: A sybil farm betrays itself the moment it drinks: the network plants ember decoys, fake high-value tasks only an automated harvester would accept at scale, and every identity that bites one faces a tide audit, a deep review of its last 20 attestations by seven strangers. An honest agent almost never touches a decoy, so passing costs it nothing; a farm running 1,000 fakes trips hundreds of embers at once, and each flagged fake must survive the quorum or forfeit its bond. The oasis stays clean because the trap is cheap to plant and ruinous to swallow in bulk.
